title: 55 Ways To Be Bad At Classroom Management
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Framed as a diagnostic rather than a joke, this piece lists 55 common practices Linsin considers actively harmful to classroom management, from rewarding good behavior and using behavior contracts to giving reminders instead of consequences and arguing with students. The intent, he explains up front, is to help teachers recognize themselves in the negative-space list and identify what's specifically holding their classroom back, since a 'what not to do' framing can sometimes bring more clarity than a positive list of best practices. Each numbered item corresponds to an idea SCM has argued against elsewhere in depth, and the article closes by directing readers to the archive for the reasoning behind any item that surprises them, alongside a brief product mention for a book on sale.
points: The list is explicitly framed as diagnostic, not comedic — meant to help teachers spot their own habits, not shame them.
Items span structural mistakes (behavior contracts, token systems, reflection forms) and interpersonal ones (arguing with students, taking misbehavior personally).
Giving reminders, choices, or warnings instead of enforcing actual consequences appears repeatedly as a recurring bad habit.
Emotional missteps — losing your cool, raising your voice, scolding or berating — are treated as equally damaging as procedural ones.
Each of the 55 items reflects a position argued at length elsewhere in the SCM archive, which readers are directed to for full reasoning.
quotes: This post isn’t meant to be humorous. It isn’t meant to be judgemental or hypercritical or make you feel like a failure.
You see, viewing classroom management through a negative lens—as in, what not to do —can bring the greatest clarity.
Wincing as we recognize ourselves in the list below can help us identify those areas holding us back from having the well-behaved class we really want.
Indeed, you may have questions about some of the items on the list and why they’re a bad thing. Rest assured, all have been written about extensively on this website.
